title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
requirement: A landlord is prohibited from terminating a residential tenancy without establishing at-fault or no-fault just cause as defined by the ordinance.
exemptions: transient occupancy, short-term rentals, deed-restricted affordable housing, government-subsidized housing (excluding Section 8), mobilehomes under state law, institutional housing, shared kitchen/bath with landlord, owner-occupied single-family residence with limited rentals, owner-occupied duplex, new construction (15 years or less), and certain alienable properties meeting specific ownership and notice criteria
interaction: The rights conferred by this Division are in addition to any existing rights provided to tenants by state or federal law.
quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.

title: Notice to Tenant of Residential Tenant Protections
requirement: A landlord of a residential rental property subject to this Division must provide written notice in no less than 12-point font regarding rent limits, local just cause termination rules, and senior or disabled tenant protections, and include a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide.

title: Relocation Assistance for Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
requirement: For no-fault just cause terminations, landlords must provide relocation assistance either via direct payment equal to two months of actual rent (or three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled) or through an equivalent rent waiver for the final months of tenancy.
key_value: 2 months of actual rent (3 months for senior or disabled)
coverage_conditions: residential rental property subject to this Division

title: Additional Requirement Upon Termination of a Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause (Right of First Refusal)
requirement: If a residential rental property is re-rented within five years after a no-fault eviction under specific sections, the landlord must first offer to lease the unit back to the displaced tenant if the tenant timely requested it in writing and provided contact information.

title: Disclosure Prior to Buyout Offers
requirement: Prior to making a buyout offer, landlords must provide each tenant a written disclosure stating their right not to enter into the agreement, consult an attorney, refuse future offers, and receive relocation assistance, among other mandated notices.

title: Requirements for Buyout Agreements
requirement: Buyout agreements must be in writing, provide a copy to each tenant at signing, include specific bold statutory notices in at least 14-point font, be provided in translated versions if negotiations occurred in a non-English language, and be for an amount greater than the required relocation assistance.
quoted_span: The landlord shall comply with the following:

title: Void Buyout Agreements
requirement: Any buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates the division and is void.
quoted_span: Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c).

title: Retaliation Prohibited
requirement: Landlords are prohibited from retaliating against a tenant for exercising any right provided by or seeking enforcement of the division.
quoted_span: A landlord shall not retaliate against a tenant for exercising any right provided by this Division or seeking the enforcement of this Division.
